# StreamDirector

> **This is an experimental test project — not a finished product.**
> The entire codebase was generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai) (Anthropic) as a proof of concept.
> Expect rough edges, missing features, and no guarantees of stability.

Lightweight multiview Twitch dashboard as a tiny Windows desktop app (2 MB).
Designed for 1920x1080 OBS window capture in live productions.

![StreamDirector Preview](preview.jpg)

## Download

Download `StreamDirector-<version>.exe` from the [latest release](https://github.com/stefanpoensgen/stream-director/releases/latest) and run it — a single file, no installation required.

Requires Windows 10 or 11 — everything else (the WebView2 browser engine and .NET Framework 4.8) is part of Windows and kept up to date by Windows Update.

> **Upgrading from 0.0.6 or older** (Electron versions): the channel list is not carried over. Use **Import** to add your channels again.

> **Windows SmartScreen:** Since the app is not code-signed, Windows Defender may show a warning on first launch. Click **"More info"** → **"Run anyway"** to proceed.

## Usage

- **Add channels** via the sidebar input or the **Import** button (paste a list, one per line). Check the [Discussions](https://github.com/stefanpoensgen/stream-director/discussions) for ready-made channel lists for upcoming events
- **Toggle** channels live with the switch in the sidebar
- **Click** a channel name to focus it (large view + audio)
- **Volume** is set per channel (slider when hovering the focus, sidebar slider or `↑`/`↓`) and remembered

## Hotkeys

| Key       | Action                            |
| --------- | --------------------------------- |
| `←` / `→` | Cycle focus through live channels |
| `↑` / `↓` | Volume of focused channel ±5 %    |
| `F`       | Recall last focused channel       |
| `S`       | Toggle sidebar                    |
| `C`       | Open chat of focused channel      |
| `F11`     | Toggle fullscreen                 |
| `Escape`  | Close import modal                |

## Window Controls

The app runs as a frameless window. Controls are in the bottom-left corner:

- **Drag** the logo area to move the window
- **Menu** toggles the sidebar
- **Login** opens the Twitch login window, which closes by itself once you are logged in. The login is used for all streams, so a Twitch Turbo subscription removes ads everywhere. While logged in, the button turns into **Logout**
- **Chat** opens the chat of the focused channel in a popup
- **Close** (✕) closes the app

Settings, channel list and Twitch login are stored in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\StreamDirector`. Delete that folder to reset the app.

## Layout

L-shape grid optimized for 1920x1080:

- **Left column** (240px): up to 7 tiles stacked vertically
- **Focus area**: remaining width, top-right
- **Bottom row**: additional tiles
- **Bottom-left cell**: branding, drag handle, menu/chat/login/close buttons

## Playback

Streams are played by a built-in HLS player ([hls.js](https://github.com/video-dev/hls.js)) instead of Twitch embeds — less than half the memory, no autoplay restrictions.

- Tiles play **360p**, the focus plays **source** quality
- Focus switches are seamless: the quality changes at the next 2-second segment boundary while playback continues — no gap in picture or sound
- Players are never reloaded or re-parented on focus switches, only CSS classes, quality and mute change
- Channels that are live but cannot be played (subscriber-only, geo-blocked) show **UNAVAILABLE** instead of OFFLINE

> Playback relies on Twitch's unofficial web API (the same one [streamlink](https://github.com/streamlink/streamlink) uses). It can break if Twitch changes it.

## Development

The app is a small C# host (`host/`) that shows the web renderer (`index.html`, `app.js`, …) in WebView2. Building needs the [.NET SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download) (8 or newer), on Windows or in WSL/Linux; running needs Windows.

```bash
# Format check (renderer)
npm install
npm run check

# Build → host/bin/Debug/net48/StreamDirector.exe
dotnet build host

# Run with DevTools (F5 reloads the page)
host/bin/Debug/net48/StreamDirector.exe --dev
```

Renderer files are embedded into the exe, so renderer changes need a `dotnet build` and an app restart.

> **WSL:** build into a Windows folder and start it from there, e.g. `dotnet build host -o /mnt/c/Users/<you>/StreamDirector-dev`. Windows may run a stale cached copy of an exe started from `\\wsl.localhost\…`.

### Architecture

```
host/                    C# WebView2 host (.NET Framework 4.8)
  MainForm.cs            Frameless window, popups, F11, version label
  AppRequestHandler.cs   Answers https://localhost/* in-process: renderer files + API
  TwitchClient.cs        Twitch API client (live status, HLS playlists)
  TwitchSession.cs       Login state (WebView2 cookie store), logout
  LoginForm.cs           Twitch login window, closes itself after login
  EmbeddedFiles.cs       Single-file support: renderer, WebView2 assemblies and loader live in the exe
  NativeMethods.cs       Win32 icon loading
index.html               App shell
app.js                   State management, layout, player lifecycle, volume, hotkeys
player.js                HLS player per channel (tile/focus quality switching)
styles.css               Dark theme, CSS Grid layout
vendor/                  Vendored hls.js (light build)
```

The release is one file: renderer, licenses and the WebView2 assemblies are embedded resources. Only the tiny native `WebView2Loader.dll` cannot run from memory — it is written once to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\StreamDirector\WebView2Loader\`.

There is no local web server: WebView2 hands every request for `https://localhost` to the host. The origin has to be `localhost` — Twitch's playlist servers reject other origins.

The renderer only talks HTTP to the host:

| Endpoint                        | Purpose                                       |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /api/live?channels=a,b`    | Which of the channels are streaming           |
| `GET /api/playlist/<name>.m3u8` | HLS master playlist (with Turbo token if any) |
| `GET /api/auth`                 | `{ "loggedIn": true/false }`                  |
| `POST /api/logout`              | Drop the Twitch session                       |

State is persisted in `localStorage`. Max 14 simultaneous players with LRU eviction.

### Dependencies

Kept to a minimum: the app has one dependency, Microsoft's `Microsoft.Web.WebView2` NuGet package. The browser engine (WebView2) and the runtime (.NET Framework 4.8) come with Windows, so their security updates arrive through Windows Update. The only npm package is `prettier` (dev only). `hls.js` is vendored (`vendor/hls.light.mjs`, currently **1.6.15**) so it only changes when deliberately updated:

```bash
npm pack hls.js@<version>
tar xzf hls.js-<version>.tgz
cp package/dist/hls.light.mjs vendor/hls.light.mjs
cp package/LICENSE vendor/hls.js.LICENSE
sed -i '/^\/\/# sourceMappingURL=/d' vendor/hls.light.mjs
```

### Release

Tag a version to trigger a GitHub Action that builds the app and attaches the exe to a new release. The app version is taken from the tag — no version bump commit needed:

```bash
git tag v1.0.0
git push --tags
```
